title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 11
statement: A paper triangle with sides of lengths \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) inches, as shown, is folded so that point \(A\) falls on point \(B.\) What is the length in inches of the crease?

solutions.text:
The crease lies along the perpendicular bisector of \(AB,\) meeting \(AC\) at \(E\) because \(AC \gt BC.\) Let \(D\) be the midpoint of \(AB,\) so \(AD = \tfrac52\) and \(\triangle ADE\) is right-angled at \(D.\) Since \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB,\) we have \(\tfrac{DE}{AD} = \tfrac{CB}{AC} = \tfrac34,\) so \[ DE = \frac52 \cdot \frac34 = \frac{15}{8}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Folding \(A\) onto \(B\) creases along the perpendicular bisector of \(AB;\) since \(AC \gt BC\) it meets \(AC\)
With \(D\) the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(E\) on \(AC,\) triangle \(ADE \sim\) triangle \(ACB,\) so \(DE = AD \cdot \tfrac{CB}{AC}\)
